pageHero.title: A practical thinking system for self-management.
pageHero.body: Red Pen Review is not simply a journaling technique. It is a structured way to externalize your thinking, organize the problem, decide the next move, and build the capacity to manage your own work and life with more clarity.

definition.title: The problem is not lack of ability. It is too much unprocessed input.
definition.body: Modern professionals are surrounded by information, emotion, other people's opinions, social media, AI output, tasks, and constant pressure. But most of us were never taught how to process all of it.
definition.body2: Red Pen Review creates a repeatable thinking process: write what is occupying the mind, review it with distance, structure the issue, decide what matters, and move into action.

materials.title: Write. Organize. Decide. Execute.
items: Write: make invisible thoughts visible on paper.
Organize: separate facts, feelings, assumptions, and noise.
Decide: identify the real question and choose the next move.
Execute: act, review, and improve the cycle.

method.title: Write. Acknowledge. Review. Move.
method.body: The daily method stays simple on purpose. It is the operating practice behind the wider Red Pen approach.

steps.title: Write
steps.text: Start with your base-colour pen. Write whatever is occupying your mind: tasks, pressure, emotion, repeated thoughts, unfinished decisions, or unclear questions.

steps.title: Acknowledge
steps.text: Read what you wrote without judging it. Notice what is present: emotion, fear, desire, obligation, pressure, reaction, or a pattern that keeps repeating.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: Pick up the red pen. Separate fact from interpretation, signal from noise, and the real issue from the surface reaction.

steps.title: Move
steps.text: Choose the next honest move. It may be a decision, a conversation, a boundary, a pause, or one clear question to carry forward.

details.title: The method can grow into a self-management system.

items.title: Level 1: Brain Dump
items.body: Everything begins by getting thoughts out of the head. Before anything can be organized, it has to become visible.

items.title: Level 2: RED PEN 15
items.body: A 15-minute review practice for reducing mental noise, identifying what actually matters, and deciding where to place attention.

items.title: Level 3: First Step Design
items.body: A method for translating organized thinking into the next clear action, so reflection does not stay abstract.

items.title: Level 4: Time Review
items.body: A way to review how time is actually being used, because time allocation often reveals what thinking has prioritized.

items.title: Level 5-7: Goal, Gap, Execution
items.body: Advanced practices for designing direction, identifying gaps, structuring issues, and building a repeatable review cycle for execution.

practice.title: From mental clarity to self-management.
practice.body: Red Pen Review starts with mental clarity, but the deeper goal is not only to feel organized. The goal is to build the capacity to think independently, manage your priorities, and move forward without waiting for someone else to define the answer.
items: Use it when your mind is busy and you cannot see what the real issue is.
Use it before decisions, meetings, goal-setting, or difficult conversations.
Use it to separate what happened from what you are assuming.
Use it as a repeatable review cycle for work, life, time, and execution.

items.q: How is Red Pen Review different from regular journaling?
items.a: Red Pen Review does not stop at expression. It helps you move from raw thoughts to review, structure, decision, and action. The goal is not only self-discovery; it is clearer self-management.

items.q: What kind of pen should I use?
items.a: Any pen that feels comfortable to write with. The key is the visual contrast between your base colour and the red — so pick whatever suits your hand and helps you write freely.

items.q: Do I need to re-read what I've written?
items.a: Not necessarily. You can write and let it go, or never revisit it at all. The act of writing and reviewing in the moment is where the value lies. Follow whatever approach feels right for you.

items.q: Why use a red pen specifically?
items.a: The red pen creates a visual separation between your raw expression and your reflective review. That contrast makes it easier to observe your own thinking from a slight distance — a small but powerful shift in perspective.

items.q: Are there any rules when starting?
items.a: None. Start simply, without overthinking. Write whatever is on your mind, as honestly as you can — including the messy or negative parts. There is no wrong way to begin.

items.q: Do I need to write every day?
items.a: No — write when you want to, when you are able to. That said, even five minutes a day can build a grounding rhythm and help settle your mind. What matters most is finding a pace that feels sustainable and enjoyable for you.

items.q: How exactly does Red Pen Review work?
items.a: Using your base-colour pen, write out what is occupying your mind. Then pick up the red pen and review what you have written. A simple four-step flow: ① Write → ② Acknowledge → ③ Review → ④ Move. The wider training system expands this into time review, goal design, gap analysis, and execution review.
